lines.en: Anna Croft remained silent throughout the journey to Oro Castle.
She occasionally gave a strange smile when our eyes met, but she never initiated a conversation.
It would have been nice to at least read her thoughts, but my understanding of Anna Croft was too low to activate stage 2 of [Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint].
Well, I hadn't particularly liked Anna Croft in the original novel either.
I wouldn't have enough fingers on both hands just to count the times Yoo Joonghyuk had been killed or betrayed by her.
With both Anna Croft and me keeping quiet, the atmosphere in the carriage rapidly grew awkward, leaving poor Selena Kim sweating buckets.
“······That's how we ended up coming together. Asgard's incarnations were invited too.”
Too kind by nature to endure this atmosphere, Selena Kim kept explaining things no one had asked about. Still, it was good for me, since I was getting all sorts of information.
“I see. Do all three of you belong to Asgard?”
“Yes. Anna arranged it.”
“You chose a good nebula.”
“Ahaha, we just happened to get lucky. Thanks to that, we get to enjoy a privilege like this. The other incarnations weren't even invited······.”

Selena Kim seemed a little excited. An invitation from the Gourmet Association did mean something different from an invitation to the Constellation Banquet. If the Constellation Banquet was a gathering of all the nobility, the Gourmet Association was more like a salon for the upper aristocracy.
But a privilege (好事), huh.
Even once Selena Kim arrived there, I doubted she would still be able to think that.
“Iris, why are you so quiet? You said you wanted to see Dokja-ssi again.”
“Blin (влин)! When did I ever!”
“Honestly······ Ever since the last banquet, it's been Dokja-nim this, Dokja-nim that, hasn't it? You finally get to see him again, so try talking to him.”
Iris's face turned bright red at Selena Kim's words, which sounded like teasing.
After stealing glances at me to gauge my reaction, Iris cautiously spoke.
“Um, you are the Demon King of Salvation······ -nim, right?”
For a moment, I wondered whether this really was the same cheeky brat from back then, but I decided to be polite too.
“I am.”
“······D-does being here with us make you uncomfortable?”
“Why would you think that?”
“We're just ordinary incarnations. And you, Demon King of Salvation-nim, are······.”
Beside her, Selena Kim's expression was changing too.
She seemed to have remembered that I was a ‘constellation’, different from them—a fact she'd briefly forgotten in her delight at seeing me.
The gap between a ‘Narrative-grade constellation’ and an ordinary ‘incarnation’ was as vast as the distance between heaven and earth.
Another constellation would probably have spouted some line like, “You insignificant insects have finally realized your place.” Of course, I wouldn't.
“It's fine. I was an incarnation once too.”
At my words, I saw Selena Kim let out a sigh of relief.
Encouraged, Iris spoke again.
“Um, then······ may I ask you a question?”
“Go ahead.”
“Do you have an incarnation under a sponsorship contract?”
“Why do you ask?”
Selena gave the hesitant Iris a pointed look.
“Iris. You already have a constellation sponsor chosen for you, don't you?”
“I-I was just asking! I'm curious!”
Watching Iris twist her twin tails around her fingers and turn her head sharply away reminded me of Shin Yoosung and Lee Gilyoung back on Earth.
I wondered if those two were doing all right······.
I spoke, doing my best to hide how much I missed them.
“My incarnation is on the Korean Peninsula.”
Iris's expression changed at my words.
“Oh, is it that little girl······?”
I nodded.
It seemed rumors about Shin Yoosung had spread elsewhere too.
Since the constellations loved gossip, they'd probably already told their own incarnations.
That was when Anna Croft spoke.
“Have you considered changing incarnations?”
Startled, Selena Kim and Iris glanced at Anna Croft.
Anna Croft continued.
“There are many excellent incarnations under the nebula <Asgard>. Many talented ones too. Iris here is one of them.”
It was an unexpected proposal.
Why was Anna Croft suddenly making an offer like this?
Perhaps they were talking about me in Asgard too.
I hadn't formally founded a ‘nebula’ yet, after all.
“Are you asking me to join <Asgard>?”

“Not necessarily. There are many excellent incarnations under Asgard, so I'm merely suggesting that choosing one of them wouldn't be a bad idea. A sponsor can withdraw a sponsorship contract at any time anyway, can't they?”
Iris, who had briefly looked dejected, gazed at me with sparkling eyes.
I answered with an expressionless face.
“I have no intention of canceling my sponsorship contract.”
“You must be quite fond of that girl. ‘Shin Yoosung’, was it?”
When I didn't answer, I saw deep disappointment spread across Iris's face.
The change in her emotions was strong enough for my skill to detect despite my very low understanding of her.
Then Anna Croft said something strange.
“Suppose that incarnation were to die suddenly······.”
An inscrutable smile rested on Anna Croft's lips.

“Don't look so surprised. I'm only giving an example. It could happen, couldn't it? An unforeseen accident, or an incarnation dying in a sudden disaster······. Such things happen all the time. Would you still have no intention of changing incarnations even if that happened?”
“An unforeseen accident, you say?”
“Yes, an unforeseen accident. An unforeseen accident that simply happened by chance.”
I stared quietly at Anna Croft.
Shin Yoosung dying······.
I'd never considered it.
“That won't happen as long as I'm alive.”
“You never know. No one knows when or how [Fate] might take effect.”
The air suddenly trembled.
The air around us took on an ominous hue, and the entire carriage shuddered.
Iris's and Selena Kim's faces were stiffening.
Goosebumps rose along the two incarnations' forearms as they looked at me in terror.
Woooooo.
I hadn't wanted to do this.
I hadn't wanted to frighten innocent incarnations as well.
But just now, Anna Croft had crossed a line she should never have crossed.
[If that happens.]
Tzzzzzzzt!
Sparks of probability began to fly as I used my True Voice.
[The constellations of the nebula <Asgard> express their concern to you.]
[The constellations of the nebula <Asgard> issue warnings to you!]
The Asgard constellations' indirect messages reached my ears. But I didn't stop using my True Voice.
[If that happens, I will destroy every world that brought about that [Fate].]
Booooom!

The shock of my erupting Status blew out all the carriage windows at once. The startled coachman was looking back at us. Even the composed Anna Croft looked faintly shocked. It seemed she hadn't known exactly how much ‘Status’ I possessed.
Before long, the carriage stopped, and we heard the guide's voice.
[We have arrived at Oro Castle.]
I grinned at the three of them, still frozen in place, and said,
“Let's get out.”
Once we stepped out of the carriage, we were led straight to Oro Castle.
Oro Castle (五輅城).
One of the Gourmet Association's principal bases scattered across all dimensions, this fortress was personally owned by one of the association's executives.
If I remembered correctly, its owner was······ probably one of the Demon Realm's 72 demon kings. Was it ‘Immeasurable Austerity’?
[These guests have been granted permission to enter.]
[Confirmed. Please come in.]
Once we entered the castle, the interior looked more modern than medieval. It reminded me of the lobby of a luxury hotel. Here and there, I spotted constellations in the form of symbolic bodies.
[Several constellations take notice of your presence.]
Our guide led us to a waiting room in a corner of the first-floor lobby.
Apparently no one else had arrived yet, since the waiting room held only me and the Asgard trio.
[Please wait here for a moment. There are still more incarnations due to arrive······ Ah, since the ‘Demon King of Salvation’-nim is a constellation, we will prepare a separate waiting room for you.]
“No, that's all right. I'll stay here.”
The guide gave me a puzzled look, but soon disappeared, apparently satisfied.
Honestly, I still felt more comfortable here.
I needed some time to prepare myself too.
As expected, panels hung on the waiting room walls for our viewing pleasure. Scenes from lower-level scenarios taking place across the dimensions even now······.
“Um, about earlier······.”
It was Selena Kim who spoke to me.
She could easily have been wary of me after what had happened in the carriage, but sure enough, the character descriptions in Ways of Survival never got anything wrong. I answered with a faint smile.
“It's all right. I went a little too far.”
Only then did Selena Kim's expression soften a little.
“No, we were terribly rude. I apologize, Demon King of Salvation.”
Her words were much more formal than before.
I hadn't meant to elicit that kind of apology, and it left me feeling uneasy.

Selena Kim hadn't done anything wrong. She was one of the few characters in all of Ways of Survival I thought well of. The one I disliked was that shameless woman standing in the corner, watching how things unfolded.
Just then, the waiting room door opened, and another guide appeared.
[Would the incarnations of Asgard please follow me.]
It seemed Asgard's constellations wanted to see them.
Selena Kim and Iris gave slight bows and left first.
Anna Croft, however, didn't immediately leave the room. She was looking at me.
“You have too many constellations as enemies.”
“That isn't your concern.”
Anna Croft's brow creased slightly at my firm answer.

Despite what had happened earlier, Anna Croft didn't seem particularly intimidated. She was merely an incarnation, but she had a contract with an entire nebula. <Asgard>'s highest-ranking incarnations were probably protecting her from my Status.
“I'm giving you sincere advice as a comrade working toward the same goal. Whether you like it or not, now is the time to cooperate with other constellations.”
The same goal······.
“Well, I don't know what your goal is, so I can't answer that.”
“Protecting this world. Isn't that what you're fighting for too?”

Instead of answering, I quietly studied the panels on the waiting room walls. Videos of incarnations being brutally torn apart by the appearance of disasters or constellations. When I didn't respond, Anna Croft walked past me.
At that moment, I spoke.
“We'll have to wait and see whether this world is worth protecting.”
Anna Croft's expression stiffened at my casually dropped remark.
She glanced anxiously between me and the guide walking ahead, then spoke with a short sigh.
“······I hope we have another opportunity to talk later.”
After she hurried away, I was alone in the waiting room.
Left by myself, I quietly gathered my thoughts.
I recalled the Gourmet Association constellations mentioned in Ways of Survival and made a mental list of those I might be able to persuade.
I didn't forget to consider their traits, likes, and dislikes either.
I'd been lucky at the Constellation Banquet, but there was no guarantee I would be again.
In terms of high society, this Gourmet Association gathering was my proper debut.
The impression I made here and the things I said would change the course of the scenarios I would shape from now on.
Then the waiting room door burst open.
I thought it might be another guide, but this time an unexpected figure was waiting for me.
Just as I was about to say something in alarm, the visitor spoke first.
[It's been a while, Kim Dokja. I've been waiting a long time.]
The moment I heard the bright tone of that True Voice, I realized who it was.
Honestly, the Queen of the Underworld was far too mischievous.
I asked with a sigh.
“······Why on earth do you look like that?”
Persephone smiled faintly.
[Why? Don't you like it? The archangel from next door has been telling everyone that this is your type.]
“That is a complete misunderstanding.”
Persephone let out a seemingly disappointed sound.
For the record, Persephone had taken on Yoo Joonghyuk's appearance.
At least she wasn't wearing a cheongsam. Thank goodness for that.
[Then how about this?]
Before I could finish trying to stop her, Persephone changed her appearance again.
As her clothing transformed into a cheongsam, I thought she was turning into Yoo Sangah again. But this time, to my surprise, it was someone I'd never expected.
“What on earth······.”
At that radiant little smile, I felt my face growing hot even though I knew it was Persephone. She had taken on the appearance of ‘the Punisher’, whom I'd seen in the Demon Realm not long ago.
[You seemed unable to take your eyes off her back then. Is this your type after all?]
At the sight of the snow-white bare skin exposed through the dress's side slit, I reflexively closed my eyes and shouted.
“······Please stop teasing me!”
[Hehe, you're so entertaining.]
Laughing like a child, Persephone transformed once more.
This time, she looked like Yoo Sangah.
A neat office outfit instead of a cheongsam or garter belt.
Seeing her like that reminded me of my days at Mino Soft, stirring complicated feelings. Yoo Sangah had always dressed that way when she came over to talk to me.
I wondered if Yoo Sangah-ssi was doing well.
I was a little worried to hear she was traveling with Han Sooyoung······ but she was ‘Yoo Sangah-ssi’, after all. I believed she'd be all right.
Persephone spoke with a bright smile.
[Come with me. I'm here to fetch you.]
I nodded and followed Persephone.
The moment I left the waiting room, several constellations' gazes bore down on me, making me a little tense. I also saw constellations whispering as they watched me with Persephone.
Somehow, I felt like a noblewoman's young attendant.
Before long, Persephone and I reached the enormous elevator in the center of the lobby.
The Gourmet Association's festival would probably take place on the fortress's top floor.
The doors of the elevator, which resembled a giant crystal ball, opened, and Persephone and I stepped inside.
With a tilting sensation, my body grew a little heavier, and the scenery of a dark dimension unfolded beyond the transparent crystal walls.
Beyond the dimension's horizon, the vast world of the <Star Stream> was revealing itself.
[You look very excited.]
“I'm more nervous than excited.”
Persephone smiled as though she understood how I felt.
[I'm glad you're alive. You were an incarnation the last time I saw you, and now you've become a constellation in your own right.]
“I'm still only a novice. I'm not sure I really belong here.”
I'd meant it as a modest remark, but whatever Persephone had heard in it, her expression had stiffened slightly.
[Do you think I lack even that much standing in the ‘Gourmet Association’? That I'd struggle to bring along a single new member?]
“That isn't what I meant······.”
[I'm joking.]
“Please stop teasing me.”
[Who knows how promising a constellation you might become? Think of this as an early investment. It's something you'll have to experience someday too.]
I'd wondered about it before, but I had no idea why this queen treated me so well.
All she'd asked in return for taking the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint to Tartarus in the Underworld was that I attend this ‘Gourmet Association’ gathering.
She probably knew too.
That even this condition of ‘attending the Gourmet Association’ would ultimately benefit me, rather than her. She had, in effect, arranged a proper debut for me now that I'd become a constellation.
Persephone's obsidian eyes sparkled.
[What level is your Status at now? Surely not Narrative-grade.]
Apparently, the other constellations hadn't learned that I was ‘Narrative-grade’. I thought for a moment before answering.
“We might see each other on the second floor at the next ‘Constellation Banquet’.”
Persephone's eyes widened.
She must have assumed my Status was Historical-grade at best.
It was rather satisfying to see the Queen of the Underworld flustered.
But deep concern soon entered her gaze.
[There will be constellations who envy you.]
[Some constellations will try to draw you over to their side.]
“I'm expecting that.”
I was prepared for it.
None of the constellations I would meet from now on would be easy to deal with.
Whether they envied me or wanted me on their side.
Either way, they would be equally dangerous.
[But most constellations won't take much interest in you.]
“······Pardon?”

[Until now, you've probably only visited places where the ‘Korean Peninsula scenarios’ have considerable influence, so you may not have noticed······ But don't forget that this is the ‘Gourmet Association’.]
The Gourmet Association.
A grand banquet where the high-ranking constellations of the <Star Stream> gathered.
Suddenly, Persephone's smile felt frightening.
[I won't play your nanny as I did at the ‘Constellation Banquet’. This time, I want to see you rise through your own strength.]
The elevator doors opened with a chime, and as though putting her words into practice, Persephone disappeared into the banquet hall. Left alone, I hesitantly stepped out of the elevator.
[Several constellations show curiosity about you.]
Several constellations turned their eyes on me the moment I stepped out, but their interest soon vanished.
That was a relief, if anything. Too much attention would have made it harder to move around.
There were no constellations in ‘symbolic bodies’ like those in the first-floor lobby.
All of them humanoid, or mimicking the forms of creatures from other worlds.
Not a single constellation here bothered with petty concerns about [probability].

Several constellations occupying the center of the noisy banquet hall looked just as I'd read about them in Ways of Survival. The first to catch my eye was a man in Viking attire at the center of the hall. It would have been stranger not to recognize him after seeing the enormous hammer strapped to his back.
[The best first-generation Story is obviously ‘Dragon Eating the Hammer’!]
‘Thursday's Thunder’, a constellation of the nebula <Asgard>, was raising his booming voice. A woman across from him answered.
[What are you talking about? The best is obviously ‘Children of Dawn’. It has the highest rating too.]
A goddess in a snow-white dress that looked embroidered with starlight.
If I remembered correctly, that woman was probably the ‘Morning Star Goddess’, a constellation of the nebula <Guardian Tree>.
Apparently, another argument had broken out over which Story was the best.

I'd heard that they were forever arguing over which Story was best, and the scene was exactly as described in Ways of Survival. Watching high-ranking constellations rarely seen on the Korean Peninsula stroll about so casually really brought home what kind of place this was.
Even the powerful ‘Persephone’ was merely an ordinary constellation in the ‘Gourmet Association’.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ cheers you on.]
My only consolation was that, thankfully, the ‘channel’ worked here.
Right. I couldn't let a place like this intimidate me.
I edged toward the groups at the center of the ‘Gourmet Association’ gathering and tried speaking to one of the constellations lingering nearby.
“Excuse me······.”
But no one turned to look at me.
Constellations acting as though I didn't exist here.
I gathered my courage and tapped the shoulder of the constellation beside me.
“Excuse me.”
This time, there was a response.
But after glancing back at me, the constellation shoved my shoulder as though picking a fight, then walked back to the center of the banquet hall.
「Kim Dokja knew this feeling very well.」
The feeling that I alone was isolated from the entire world.
Suddenly, all those constellations' voices felt distant.
We were clearly in the same place, yet they were somewhere else.
Only then did I understand the ‘indifference’ Persephone had spoken of.
The ‘Gourmet Association’ had built a sturdy wall of its own, keeping newcomers like me from casually setting foot inside.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ looks at you with pity.]
······But I couldn't give up like this.
I had to find a way to create an opening.
I looked farther afield, examining the edges of the Gourmet Association gathering.

Apart from the constellations chatting in the center of the banquet hall, I could see others wandering about alone. They were also members of the ‘Gourmet Association’, so they must have been powerful constellations too.
At the edge of the banquet hall, countless panels covered the walls, incomparably larger than those in the waiting room.
Videos of ‘scenarios’ taking place all over the world.
Looking closely, I found a small display in one corner showing the moment I'd become the ‘Demon King of Salvation’.
But no constellation was watching it.
Even the ‘Korean Peninsula scenarios’ I'd experienced were merely one passing story here.
The panel beside it showed a live feed of the Korean Peninsula.
It seemed to be Bihyung's channel.
On the screen, a self-proclaimed beautiful girl with bobbed hair was spouting nonsense.
―That bastard Kim Dokja is definitely having the time of his life right now.
The familiar voice made me chuckle.
Han Sooyoung, you wouldn't be saying that crap if you knew where I was right now.
―Hey, you're collecting those Abyssal Stones, right? Make sure you gather plenty. If things go wrong later, we'll at least have to use those.
―······Did Dokja-ssi really ask you to do this?
―I told you he did!
Watching Han Sooyoung and Yoo Sangah bicker on the screen filled me with longing. I felt that watching any longer would only make me miserable, so I turned to the next panel.
That panel showed a typical ‘mass-produced Story’.
The Story was titled 「Legend of the Legendary Return from Another World」.

The title alone reeked of third-rate fiction, and the plot was just as predictable: a returnee from another world saved the world, and everyone became happy. Still, it was watchable. There was something about it that resembled Ways of Survival······ Somehow, even the protagonist spoke like Yoo Joonghyuk. After I'd given the Story a quick look, a message appeared.
[Would you like to submit a star rating?]
Oh, so this was a system for rating each Story.
I cautiously placed my hand on the ‘star rating’ field beside the work.
Just then, I heard someone's voice.
[This is my favorite Story.]
I turned around to find an old man standing there.
I gave a slight bow and answered.
“It was an interesting story.”
[Hoho, wasn't it? You're a fellow with a discerning eye.]
In truth, the Story didn't particularly suit the ‘Gourmet Association’ as I knew it.
The association's constellations didn't like mass-produced Stories like this.
The constellations of the ‘Gourmet Association’ were refined sorts who recoiled and started retching whenever concepts like the ‘Ninth Circle’ or ‘sword masters’ appeared.
Yet 「Legend of the Legendary Return from Another World」 featured both.
“Are you the one who submitted this Story?”
[I am. Hahaha. I submit it every year. I want even one more person to know about it. It's so good, such an entertaining Story, but I just don't know how to put it into words.]
“I understand how you feel.”
Somehow, I was even glad to meet him.

Back when I was avidly reading Ways of Survival, I'd posted recommendations for it on every community site I visited. Mostly, I'd just gotten shitloads of abuse······ Anyway, this old man seemed to be in a similar situation.
The old man added with a sigh.
[No matter how much I recommend it, the fellows here only scoff. Young things, and already so fussy······ All they ever do is go on about first-generation Stories.]
The more he said, the more surprising his remarks became.
The ‘Gourmet Association’ did have its stodgy side.
In the <Star Stream>, that tendency grew stronger the higher one's position.
Then I heard some passing constellations mutter.
[That Steady Person is back again.]
[Tsk, tsk. They say he's gone senile and can't even recognize a good Story anymore······.]
······Steady Person?
Judging by the old man's fury beside me, it seemed to be his nickname.
Steady Person. I thought there'd been a constellation with a similar nickname in Ways of Survival······.
[Piss off, you bastards! I didn't put this Story out for you lot to stuff your faces with!]
Just then, with a beep, I saw the star rating beside 「Legend of the Legendary Return from Another World」 change.
The already low rating had fallen further.
It was obvious who had done it.
[Th-those bastards!]
It was what people called ‘rating bombing’.
The old man shouted at the top of his lungs at the constellations as they walked away, sneering.
Somehow, I felt I understood how he felt. I placed my hand on the rating field and said,
“I don't think this Story is bad enough to deserve a score like that.”
A beep, and the star rating rising.
The shouting old man turned to look at me.

“Honestly, I don't really understand why Stories need scores in the first place. Every Story has value in its own way. A story that's merely entertainment to one person can be salvation to someone else.”
The old man looked startled at my words.
His lips moved a few times before he murmured with what seemed to be sincere admiration.
[You're unlike the young constellations these days······ To have such fine principles······.]
“It's nothing.”
Anyone who'd endured their childhood through a story like Ways of Survival would come to think as I did. His mood apparently much improved, the old man gave an easy chuckle.
[Well, well. It seems I've found a good fellow to talk to. What's your modifier? With everything going on, I haven't even asked.]
This seemed to be going rather well, didn't it?
I grinned and said,
[I am the Demon King of Salvation.]
At my words, a variety of expressions crossed the old man's face.
[······Demon King of Salvation······?]
It was difficult to read his precise emotions from the strange folds of his wrinkles.

At first, the old man looked unimpressed. Then he seemed faintly surprised, wore a curiously angry expression, and finally appeared admiring. More precisely, all those emotions were contained in a single expression.
[I see. So you're the one······ Hoho, I see.]
He spoke as though he knew me.
Persephone had said the Gourmet Association's constellations wouldn't know much about someone like me, so I hadn't expected anything······ Was I better known than I'd thought?
“May I ask your modifier?”
Instead of answering my question, the old man gave an inscrutable smile.
[Do you like the coat I made?]
“······Pardon?”
[The coat you're wearing.]
Without thinking, I looked down at my white coat.
[Infinite Dimension Space Coat].
It was the coat I'd received as a reward after defeating Myung Ilsang some time ago.
And the name of the constellation who had made this coat was······.
“······Mass Production Maker?”
The old man grinned at the shock in my voice.
[That's what they call me, yes.]
Watching him point proudly at himself with his thumb left me a little overwhelmed.
Mass Production Maker.
Whenever people listed the constellations capable of exerting the greatest influence over the <Star Stream>'s scenarios, he was always mentioned.
A formidable presence thanks to his close connections with countless nebulas and the Bureau alone, even if his personal combat strength could hardly be called top-tier.
To make matters worse, while clearing the fifth scenario, I'd killed the returnee Myung Ilsang, the ‘Mass Production Maker’'s incarnation.
[Hoho, no need to look like that. I'm not going to eat you.]
The ‘Mass Production Maker’ seemed to have already guessed what I was about to say.
[I know what you're thinking. Don't worry about it. It's a common occurrence in the <Star Stream>. I wasn't particularly interested in the fellow to begin with.]
[He had no grit, a weak will, and always chose the easy path. I never much liked him.]
I felt a complicated mixture of emotions.
Relief that the ‘Mass Production Maker’ wasn't particularly bothered by it, and disillusionment that, in the end, even a constellation like him regarded incarnations as nothing more than tools······.
I spoke, trying to sound composed.
“Thank you.”
[Don't thank me for that. However worthless he was, he was my incarnation. ······Anyway, I enjoyed the story you made.]
“The story I made?”
[Yes. You have a remarkable knack for taking scenarios in unexpected directions and turning them into utter chaos. Thanks to you, I had plenty to watch for a while. I gave it five stars too.]
I couldn't tell whether it was praise or sophisticated mockery, but I thanked him for now.
[This must be your first time here. Who introduced you?]
“The Queen of the Underworld.”
A curious gleam crossed the Mass Production Maker's eyes.
[That old hag······ Hehe, she's finally gone and done it. Bringing a newcomer like you here at a time like this······.]
I thought I had some idea what he meant, but deliberately played dumb.
“Is something happening in the Gourmet Association?”

[Something's always happening. More importantly, did that old hag abandon a first-time newcomer and go off to attend to her own business? Tsk, tsk······ Those Olympus bastards, honestly. Come along. I'll make a few introductions.]
Things were going better than I'd expected.
I trailed closely behind the ‘Mass Production Maker’ as he walked ahead, looking all around me.
I couldn't let all the fascinating sights make me forget why I'd come.
Ultimately, I was here to recruit constellations who would help with the ‘Demon King Selection’.
Let's see.
The best constellation to approach first would be······.
[You can tell who that drunkard over there is just by looking at him, can't you? That's ‘Thor’. That uptight-looking girl over there is ‘Vakarine’······.]

Every time the ‘Mass Production Maker’ carelessly called out a constellation's true name, a chill ran through my chest. A constellation's true name had the power to draw their attention. The problem was that you never knew whether that attention would be friendly or furious. I'd occasionally called constellations such as Persephone by their true names too, but never so recklessly······.
[I'm not particularly close to them, so don't expect much of an introduction. They recoil whenever I so much as approach.]
Indeed, ‘Thursday's Thunder’ and the ‘Morning Star Goddess’ seemed to be edging away simply because the ‘Mass Production Maker’ had appeared.
I could more or less guess why.
[Tsk, tsk. Those bastards can't even recognize a good Story······.]

Anyway, I could feel a marked difference in the constellations' reactions simply from accompanying the ‘Mass Production Maker’. The ease with which we'd entered the center of the banquet hall, where I'd struggled even to set foot earlier, was proof enough.
But at this rate, everyone would run away before I could even speak to them······.
Oh, come to think of it, ‘Asmodeus’ was also a member of the Gourmet Association······ Where was he?
[Looks like the main event is about to begin.]
The ‘Mass Production Maker’, who'd been doing all the talking, beamed and pulled me along by my sleeve. The moment we sat at a nearby table, an attendant brought us food.
[Eyes of the Ninth Circle Great Sage Merbatos]
